items.title: Netflix continues NFL evolution with start to Thanksgiving tentpole window
items.summary: Netflix and the NFL are launching Thanksgiving Eve football with Rams v Packers, pitched as a new holiday tradition for a night when people go out and reconnect. Netflix is working with EverPass, DAZN for Business and DirecTV for Business to get the game into bars and restaurants, while sources say at-home TV usage that night is no lower than a typical November Wednesday. U2 plays halftime, and Netflix already has four games set for 2027, including a Thanksgiving Eve return.
items.what_it_means: Streamers are creating new holiday windows and taking them to the venues where people gather, beyond the living room.

items.title: Data drive: Ally report shows fan spending on women's sports grows
items.summary: Ally has released its second Cost of Fandom report, finding fan spending on women's sports rising and narrowing the gap with men's sports, where spending held steady at $950. Gen Z is driving the growth, putting 34% of its sports spending into women's sports, compared with 13% for Boomers.
items.what_it_means: Younger fans are directing a much larger share of their sports wallet to women's sport than older fans do.

items.title: 'Our category felt dusty': Why Strauss now spends a third of its marketing budget on sponsorship
items.summary: German workwear brand Strauss ended its sponsorship of the German national team at the end of 2025 and in September became UEFA's first official referee partner, adding to its Europa League and Conference League deals. Chief executive Henning Strauss says the brand no longer needs to buy awareness at home and is shifting budget to growth markets such as the UK, Australia and North America. Sponsorship now accounts for about a third of a marketing budget he puts at a few hundred million euros, and he acknowledges the referee deal carries some risk given fans' views of VAR.
items.what_it_means: A challenger brand is using sport sponsorship to buy relevance in new markets rather than defend awareness it already owns.

items.title: Podcast palooza and other NWSL championship takeaways
items.summary: Around the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., digital media properties brought their online audiences together in person, with Just Women's Sports and Men in Blazers both holding paid live podcast recordings to sold-out crowds, presented by Amazon Prime and CarMax respectively. Shows linked to Togethxr, iHeartRadio, Vox Media and Footballco were also on site, including at the Ally House space and the league's Fan Fest. JWS chief executive Haley Rosen says championship weekend can now be the centrepiece of sponsorship packages after years of convincing brands.
items.what_it_means: Media brands are turning a league's marquee weekend into paid live events and sponsor inventory of their own.

items.title: Super Bowl LXI Coming to IMAX As Disney Expands Distribution
items.summary: ESPN, the NFL and IMAX have agreed to show Super Bowl LXI live in hundreds of US IMAX cinemas on 14 February 2027, a first for the game, plus select international markets including Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. It will be the largest live event in IMAX's history. Disney says it wants to reach fans across an unprecedented range of platforms, adding to an already wide set of viewing options.
items.what_it_means: The biggest broadcast in sport is being sold as a ticketed out-of-home experience as well as a TV event.

items.title: NWSL regular season viewership dropped 19%, but early playoff figures were up
items.summary: NWSL regular-season viewership fell 19% across ESPN, ABC, ESPN2, ION and CBS, with 98 measured matches averaging about 173,000 viewers after 20 games were added to the inventory. Adults 18-34 made up 11.1% of the audience, the best share under the current deals. Quarterfinal and semifinal playoff games averaged 494,000, up 13%, with 18-34 viewers up 95%, and the league has one season left on its national deals, with IMG advising on talks.
items.what_it_means: More inventory diluted the average audience, while marquee games and younger viewers grew ahead of a rights negotiation.

items.title: NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL Valuations Outpace Surge in American Wealth
items.summary: A J.P. Morgan report finds big four franchise valuations have compounded at about 12% a year since 2000, ahead of the S&P 500 (about 6.8%) and the top 0.1% wealth bracket (7.3%), driven mainly by scarcity, with only four teams added between 2000 and 2025. The number of US billionaires rose from 243 to 902 between 2002 and 2025, but rising valuations have narrowed the pool able to buy control of a team alone.
items.what_it_means: Scarcity keeps pushing team values beyond what single owners can fund, shaping who buys and how.

items.title: Inside Hershey's push for movie magic
items.summary: Hershey, a film about Milton Hershey that took about five years to produce, is the latest brand and entertainment crossover, with the company involved in scriptwriting, holding veto rights over casting and having staff on set every day. An executive says it is not a 90-minute commercial. Alongside the release, Hershey is bringing back five-cent pricing for one day on 25 November and rolling out vintage packaging.
items.what_it_means: Brands are moving from sponsoring entertainment to producing it, with retail tie-ins around the release.

items.title: Top Tours: Ed Sheeran's 'Loop Tour' Grosses More Than $120M In North America
items.summary: Ed Sheeran finished the North American leg of his Loop Tour with a sold-out stadium show in Tampa on 7 November, adding $120.6 million to the tour's gross according to figures reported to Pollstar. The 2026 world tour now stands at $232.6 million from just under 1.9 million tickets across 49 concerts, with a Latin American stadium run to finish by 11 December.
items.what_it_means: Stadium touring by a single global act continues to generate sport-scale box office.

items.title: SailGP Adds UAE Team as It Enters New Era of Private Ownership
items.summary: SailGP is adding a 14th franchise, representing the United Arab Emirates, the first in the league's era of fully independent team ownership after eight years of overhauling its model. The team is majority owned by former Vitol executive Chris Bake, with Mubadala Capital taking a minority stake and SailGP retaining a share. The UAE hosted two stops this season, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
items.what_it_means: A newer league is using host markets and outside investors to build franchise value.
